title: Position Bias Correction is Insufficient for One-Pass Attention Sorting

contributions.purpose: Enable single-pass document reordering that aims to match expensive iterative attention sorting.
contributions.mechanism: Debiased One-Pass Attention Sorting: estimate a per-prompt position-bias curve b(p) from distractor documents (trim top-alpha=0.05 by attention, bin remaining positions into B=20 bins, take median attention, interpolate) and subtract it from raw attention scores (additive s_i = a_i - b(p_i) or divisive), requiring only 2 prefill passes.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on SynthWiki@28K with two models; matches k=1 attention sorting cost (2 prefills) vs 6 prefills for k=5.
contributions.domain: Long-context retrieval / document reranking for RAG
contributions.source_quote: First, we propose and evaluate debiased one-pass attention sorting, a method that estimates and removes position bias from attention scores to enable single-pass document reordering.

contributions.purpose: Test whether position bias is the primary bottleneck limiting single-pass sorting.
contributions.mechanism: Compare debiased k=1 against uncalibrated k=1 and k=5 iterative sorting on a well-tuned model (LLaMA-2-7B-32K-Instruct) and a high-bias model (YaRN-Llama-2-7b-64k).
contributions.evaluation: On LLaMA-2-7B-32K-Instruct, debiasing gives byte-identical results to uncalibrated k=1 (94.83%, 0 wins/600 ties/0 losses); k=1 to k=5 gap is only 0.67pp.
contributions.domain: Position bias analysis in long-context LLMs
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate that position bias is not the primary bottleneck limiting single-pass sorting on well-tuned models, as evidenced by zero improvement from debiasing on LLaMA-2-7B-32K-Instruct.

contributions.purpose: Identify what iterative sorting provides beyond position-bias correction.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze accuracy and gold-document position across sorting iterations, and measure the residual gap after debiasing on the high-bias model.
contributions.evaluation: On YaRN, debiasing improves +8.67pp over uncalibrated k=1 (55.83% vs 47.17%) but remains 14.84pp behind k=5 (70.67%), closing only 37% of the gap; iterative gains attributed to attention context refinement and error reduction.
contributions.domain: Mechanistic analysis of iterative attention sorting
contributions.source_quote: Third, we identify that iterative sorting provides benefits beyond bias correction, likely from attention context refinement and error reduction, suggesting future work should investigate these mechanisms.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work builds on Attention Sorting but investigates whether explicit position-bias correction can reduce the number of required sorting iterations.

We resolve the incompatibility by adapting the overlap-set technique... Attention Sorting (Peysakhovich & Lerer, 2023) addresses position bias through iterative document reordering based on attention patterns.

We hypothesize that iterative sorting is primarily needed because raw attention scores are confounded by position bias... If we can explicitly estimate and subtract this position-dependent bias from attention scores, a single sorting pass should suffice to match iterative sorting accuracy.

notes: Negative/refutation result: the proposed debiasing hypothesis is refuted; zero effect on the well-tuned model (byte-identical to uncalibrated k=1) and insufficient (closes only 37% of gap) on the high-bias model. Authors note limitations of only two models and one benchmark.
